'Calculation Breakdown:' shows '({cgpa} - {offset}) × {multiplier} = {pct}%' for UIET else '{cgpa} × {multiplier or custom} = {pct}%'.
Eligibility list (each row shows 'Requirement: {minCgpa} · {note}' and a pill 'Eligible for Drives ✓' (green) or 'Borderline / Skills Critical' (amber)): Tier-1 eligible if cgpa>=7; Mass recruiters eligible if pct>=60 OR cgpa>=6.5; Startups always eligible.

faqs.q: Why is 9.5 used as the multiplier for CGPA to Percentage?
faqs.a: The multiplier 9.5 was statistically established by CBSE and AICTE after analyzing the performance of thousands of students across India. While the maximum CGPA is 10, the top scorers rarely score 100% in all subjects (averaging around 95%). Hence, multiplying by 9.5 provides the most statistically accurate equivalent percentage.

faqs.q: What is the official formula for IKGPTU (Uttar Pradesh Technical University)?
faqs.a: IKGPTU officially follows the AICTE guideline: Percentage = CGPA × 9.5. For example, if your B.Tech or BCA cumulative grade is 7.8, your official PTU percentage is 7.8 × 9.5 = 74.10%.

faqs.q: How do I calculate overall CGPA from semester SGPAs?
faqs.a: To calculate overall CGPA, take the sum of your Semester Grade Point Averages (SGPAs) across all completed semesters and divide by the total number of semesters (or calculate weighted credit points if course credits vary per semester). Our calculator includes a built-in semester calculator for this.

faqs.q: What if my percentage is below 60%? Can I still get an IT job?
faqs.a: Yes! While some mass recruiters maintain a 60% cutoff, modern tech startups, product firms, and techcadd's 800+ hiring partners prioritize GitHub code repositories, practical problem-solving, and live project experience. Completing our 6 Months Industrial Training program bridges any academic gap with industry-grade portfolio projects.

faqs.q: How does Panjab University (PU Lucknow) convert CGPA to percentage?
faqs.a: Panjab University departments generally follow the standard 10-point conversion (Percentage = CGPA × 10). However, specific engineering divisions such as UIET have historically recognized the formula Percentage = (CGPA - 0.75) × 10. Our calculator supports both options.
